brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two tall fused bases (0,0 and 1,0, 2 storeys each) each hold a deep bin, staged with a fork and spoon upright-leaning in one bin (prop:1, prop:2) and a knife in the other (prop:3), visible from above.
bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full-x2 and bin:1,0,1~hex-bin-full-x2 (Bin, full depth, 2 stories deep), one per cell. Solid (non-drained) floors chosen so water does not pass through.

The configurator checks fit and collisions only and knows nothing about materials or waterproofing; the parts are 3D printed in a material the user chooses. The solid bin floors help the shape retain water, but no waterproof property can be verified or claimed.
Dishwasher/heat safety depends on the print material and process, which the configurator cannot see or check; it cannot be verified or claimed here.

finish.summary: Built a two-bin utensil holder: two side-by-side 2-storey fused hex bases (cells 0,0 and 1,0), each with a deep solid-floored bin (hex-bin-full-x2) tall enough for utensils, joined as one body per storey, open faces capped and joints locked. Staged with a fork and spoon in one bin and a knife in the other; check_build passes with meshClash clear. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe could not be met or verified: those depend on the user's chosen print material, which the configurator does not model — the solid (non-drained) bins were chosen so the shape itself holds water rather than draining it.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
